verdict.probe_answer: The memo correctly identified import-binding narrowing as a real mechanism to extend and recognized that naive fuzzy import matching needed tightening. But its actual recommendation was to ship same-directory/same-module Exact first, which is the approach the settled outcome rejected as unsound for Python/JS because sibling files are not in scope unless imported. Its shadowing guard addresses one false-positive mode, but misses the decisive scope rule that made A invalid.
verdict.rationale: Vindicated shape was B: import-qualified/binding-based narrowing with fail-open behavior, and explicit rejection of same-dir/same-package Exact. This memo instead makes A the primary thin slice, adds a SameModule rung, and treats it as safe after shadow checks. That would have sent the team into implementing the unshipped, unsound design before the landed import-member rung.
